interpretations.plain_english_summary: This was a House passage vote on a bill about the Small Business Administration's rulemaking costs. It would require the SBA to keep its annual small-business regulatory budget at zero or below.
interpretations.yea_meaning: A Yea vote supported passing the bill and requiring the SBA to offset or avoid net new small-business regulatory costs each fiscal year.
interpretations.nay_meaning: A Nay vote opposed passing that SBA regulatory-budget requirement.
interpretations.policy_effect: The bill defines the small-business regulatory budget as the cost to small businesses from SBA rulemaking, including new rules and changes or repeals of existing rules. The practical effect would be to limit net new SBA regulatory costs for small businesses unless offset elsewhere.
interpretations.interpretation_reason: Manual gold-slice review used the House passage question and Congress.gov summary to describe the rulemaking-cost mechanism without inferring motive.

interpretations.plain_english_summary: This was a vote on agreeing to the Senate-amended version of a funding package after a shutdown. It combined temporary funding for most federal agencies through January 30, 2026, with full-year FY2026 funding for agriculture, military construction and veterans affairs, and legislative branch programs.
interpretations.yea_meaning: A Yea vote supported agreeing to the Senate-amended funding package and sending that version forward.
interpretations.nay_meaning: A Nay vote opposed agreeing to the Senate-amended funding package.
interpretations.policy_effect: The bill would end the shutdown that began on October 1, 2025, provide back pay to unpaid federal employees, pause federal reduction-in-force actions through January 30, 2026, fund most agencies temporarily at FY2025 levels with exceptions, and extend several expiring health, agriculture, cybersecurity, veterans, FDA, and Defense Production Act authorities.
interpretations.interpretation_reason: Manual gold-slice review distinguished the Senate-amendment concurrence vote from earlier passage and summarized the main funding effects from Congress.gov.

interpretations.plain_english_summary: This was a House passage vote on a short-term funding bill. It would keep most federal agencies funded through November 21, 2025, or until regular appropriations bills were enacted.
interpretations.yea_meaning: A Yea vote supported passing the short-term funding bill.
interpretations.nay_meaning: A Nay vote opposed passing the short-term funding bill.
interpretations.policy_effect: The bill would prevent a government shutdown at the start of FY2026 by continuing most programs at FY2025 levels with exceptions. Congress.gov also describes added security funding for federal officials, authority for D.C. local spending, and extensions of several public health, Medicare, Medicaid, veterans, agriculture, cybersecurity, unmanned-aircraft, human-trafficking assessment, whistleblower, and Defense Production Act authorities.
interpretations.interpretation_reason: Manual gold-slice review used the initial Congress.gov summary for the pre-shutdown continuing-resolution vote.

interpretations.uncertainty_note: This was a motion to instruct conferees, not final passage of the underlying appropriations bill. The available packet does not include enough official detail to describe the exact conference instruction as a source-grounded policy effect.
interpretations.interpretation_reason: Manual gold-slice review left this as ambiguous because the bill summary describes the underlying appropriations bill, while the roll call was on a conference instruction.

interpretations.plain_english_summary: This was House passage of an FY2026 appropriations bill for military construction, the Department of Veterans Affairs, and related agencies.
interpretations.yea_meaning: A Yea vote supported passing the FY2026 military construction and veterans affairs funding bill.
interpretations.nay_meaning: A Nay vote opposed passing that funding bill.
interpretations.policy_effect: The bill would fund Defense Department military construction and family housing, the NATO Security Investment Program, military housing funds, VA benefits and health programs, the National Cemetery Administration, VA administration, the American Battle Monuments Commission, the U.S. Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims, Army cemetery expenses, and the Armed Forces Retirement Home.
interpretations.interpretation_reason: Manual gold-slice review used House passage wording and the Congress.gov appropriations summary.

interpretations.plain_english_summary: This was House passage of a bill changing eligibility and application requirements for SBA 7(a) and 504 small-business loans.
interpretations.yea_meaning: A Yea vote supported passing the bill and adding the new SBA loan eligibility and certification requirements.
interpretations.nay_meaning: A Nay vote opposed passing those SBA loan eligibility and certification requirements.
interpretations.policy_effect: The bill would require SBA loan applications to include date of birth and a certification that the applicant or all beneficial owners are U.S. citizens, nationals, or lawful permanent residents. It would make several categories ineligible for those loans, including asylees, refugees, visa holders, nonimmigrants, DACA recipients, and people without lawful immigration status.
interpretations.interpretation_reason: Manual gold-slice review used the official passage vote and Congress.gov summary to describe the SBA loan eligibility mechanism.

interpretations.plain_english_summary: This was a vote on the Senate-amended version of the same budget blueprint. It kept the FY2025-FY2034 budget framework moving and advanced reconciliation instructions for later tax, spending, deficit, and debt-limit legislation.
interpretations.yea_meaning: A Yea vote supported concurring in the Senate-amended budget framework and moving those reconciliation instructions forward.
interpretations.nay_meaning: A Nay vote opposed concurring in the Senate-amended budget framework and those reconciliation instructions.
interpretations.policy_effect: The resolution directed committees to write follow-up legislation affecting deficits over FY2025-FY2034, set recommended levels for revenues and spending categories, and allowed a statutory debt-limit increase by specified amounts. Congress.gov notes that one Ways and Means instruction could allow up to a $4.5 trillion deficit increase unless other committees produced at least $2 trillion in net deficit reduction.
interpretations.interpretation_reason: Manual gold-slice review retained the budget punch-up standard for the Senate-amendment concurrence vote.

interpretations.plain_english_summary: This was a budget blueprint, not a final agency funding law. It set Congress's FY2025 budget framework and opened a reconciliation process for later tax, spending, deficit, and debt-limit legislation.
interpretations.yea_meaning: A Yea vote supported adopting the budget framework and starting the reconciliation instructions tied to later budget legislation.
interpretations.nay_meaning: A Nay vote opposed adopting that budget framework and those reconciliation instructions.
interpretations.policy_effect: The resolution directed 11 House committees to write follow-up legislation affecting deficits over FY2025-FY2034, set recommended levels for revenues and spending categories, and allowed a statutory debt-limit increase by specified amounts. Congress.gov notes that one Ways and Means instruction could allow up to a $4.5 trillion deficit increase unless other committees produced at least $2 trillion in net deficit reduction.
interpretations.interpretation_reason: Manual gold-slice review retained the budget punch-up standard for the original House budget-resolution vote.
